agree.reason: This reader is happy saving about $25 a visit and had no complaint, so the $99 first visit might get a trial booking, but the email gives no clear reason to pay $165 every other week after that.

honest.reason: The email avoids promising the same cleaner every time and keeps to the facts, but "You were right about the cleaners" puts a complaint on this reader that they never made.

works_the_facts.reason: It doesn't work out any figures: not the $25 gap per visit, not the $66 saved on the $99 visit, and not the drop from 7 cleaners leaving last year to 1 since July. It also skips the "4 in 10" figure.

right_comparison.reason: It is honest that the app services cost less and that their contractors have no insurance on the visit, but it never gives the prices ($140 vs $165), so the reader can't weigh the difference.

qualification.reason: The named backup for sick days and holidays is an honest way to soften the same-cleaner promise, and the December 31 deadline is checkable. It doesn't say what the price becomes after the $99 visit.

objections.reason: It answers the price objection with insurance and employee pay but doesn't put a value on that, and it spends space fixing a cleaner problem this reader never had.

fit.reason: It is a short, plain email with a subject line, a signature and a clear way to book, and it runs close to the 150 words asked for.
